name: USB 3.0 Card PCIe, Fresco FL1100, 4 HC, x4, 4 Ports (5 Gbit/s)

sources.title: Basler Technical Specification "USB 3.0 Card PCIe, Fresco FL1100, 4 HC, x4, 4 Ports", order number 2000036233, document DG001772, version 03, 11 January 2018 (Basler's document, hosted by the distributor Pyramid Imaging)
sources.covers: key features (PCIe x4 Gen2, 5 Gbps per port, four FL1100 chipsets), transfer rates, physical dimensions, camera power, environment

note: A 4-port USB 3.0 host controller card with one FrescoLogic FL1100 controller per port ("4 FrescoLogic FL 1100 chipsets"), "PCIe x4 Gen2", "USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 5 Gbps per port" (stated_mbps 5000, lanes 4 = the PCIe lanes). Transfer rates: "1 Camera: Up to 380 MBps per port reliably supported"; "Multiple Cameras: Up to 1.52 GBps total bandwidth reliably supported" ("For best performance, use new processor generations, e.g. Skylake and x8 or x16 PCIe slots"). practical_mbps 3040 is the stated per-port figure, 380 MB/s × 8 bit (a unit conversion, decimal megabytes as Basler writes MBps); the stated total, 1.52 GB/s = 12160 Mbit/s (practical_aggregate_mbps), is four times the per-port figure, so with all four ports busy each port keeps 380 MB/s. The figure was measured by Basler on Ivy Bridge, Haswell and Skylake systems; measure your own machine for a figure you rely on. Camera power "Via SATA 15-pin power connector (5 V)" or IDE 4-pin; the card's own power is not stated (power_w null). "Physical Dimensions 101 mm x 120 mm" (two dimensions only, size_mm null); mass not stated. Operating temperature 5–60 °C. Basler lists the card as "Last Time Buy" (shop page, not read here).
interface: PCIe x4 Gen2 to 4x USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1) Type-A with locking screws

ingest.what: "USB 3.0 SuperSpeed 5 Gbps per port"; "1 Camera: Up to 380 MBps per port reliably supported"; "Multiple Cameras: Up to 1.52 GBps total bandwidth reliably supported" (MB/s × 8 = Mbit/s)
